source_excerpts.text:
Dots Astra read-only, Today 2:10 PM local, observed 2026-11-01 approximately 04:42 UTC.

Two further proof-and-code packages have passed review. I’m saving them to Space: one avoids enumerating every boundary configuration when acquiring the stability constants; the other covers changing reaction rates within stated bounds.

The ZIPs are attached. The first makes acquisition of the scalar constants polynomial in input size; evaluating the full certificate can still be expensive. The second gives bounds under predictable rate changes, but its conservative numerical costs do not yet establish practical advantage. The deeper construction is now addressing delayed return: even a stable reaction network can trap material away from its removal channel long enough to defeat our previous proof form. I’m developing a time-resolved mechanism that pays for that delay and every intervening reaction. Its final stability guarantee is still open.

Visible attachments:
Stochastic_Multiface_Scalar_Acquisition_ACCEPTED_20261101.zip
Astra_Reviewed_Common_Predictable_Rate_Resources_20261101.zip
